rounds.fact: TypePad positioned itself as a more polished, professional blogging platform than free competitors, aimed at users willing to pay for more design control.
The Wall was a single editable text field in the earliest versions. 2007's platform launch brought app chaos, sheep-throwing included, before the News Feed took over the world.
Tom's Hardware built its reputation on exhaustive PC component benchmarks, becoming one of the go-to sites for hardware enthusiasts well before mainstream tech blogs existed.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
Tumblr popularized the short-form 'microblogging' format, and grew so fast in its early years that it regularly had to fight off downtime from its own success.
